items.title: To understand how war abroad impacts Australia, look to the price of milk
items.description: This century's biggest oil shock is entering its sixth month, with no end in sight as war in Iran continues. Is it showing up in your daily budget?

items.title: Trump's Saudi deal highlights insanity of the situation in the Middle East
items.description: It's not just that some of the strongmen don't seem so strong anymore. It's that there is a new conflation of factors proving to be just as important, if not more so, in driving world events in increasingly disturbing directions.

items.title: How the Trump administration runs Venezuela and takes its money
items.description: Amid the fallout of devastating twin earthquakes Donald Trump says the US has been taking "billions and billions of dollars from Venezuela". So who is running the country and what is happening with the seized funds?

items.title: Palestinians long for peace but doubt Trump's deal with Hamas will hold
items.description: Palestinians in Gaza have expressed scepticism about Hamas's declaration it will lay down its weapons in a bid to kickstart the stalled peace process, concerned it will not actually change the situation in the war-ravaged strip.

items.title: Spain says Ceuta migrant surge largely reversed as most return to Morocco
items.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has blamed trafficking gangs as Spanish authorities say at least 57 bodies have been recovered.

items.title: Live: 'Disappointed' but 'OK' Kennedy snags silver, teen grabs surprise gold
items.description: Flag bearer Nina Kennedy settles for silver in the pole vault and Australia's sprint stars return to the track after a host of medals at the velodrome. Follow live.

items.title: A week of AUKUS double-speak leaves everyone scratching their heads
items.description: This week's back-and-forth over AUKUS adds to the hubbub in June about whether it was a major setback that Australia's future Virginia Class submarines will be used US boats rather than some fresh off the construction dock.

items.title: The Labor MPs chasing promotions after Vic leadership spill
items.description: New Victorian Premier Ben Carroll is expected to announce his new-look ministry on Monday, with a handful of Labor MPs now jostling for promotions following the resignation of Jacinta Allan.

items.title: Alan Jones's 'anxious wait' for his day in court is over. Here's what to expect
items.description: After significant media attention, more than 70 witnesses are set to give evidence during the judge-only trial at the Downing Centre in Sydney's CBD.

items.title: How a Sydney band became massive in wartime Ukraine
items.description: Sydney band breathe. managed to become the only international act at Kyiv's Atlas music festival. What they is etched in their collective memories.

items.title: Cyclone's cool water revives 90 per cent of reef island's bleached coral
items.description: Cyclone Alfred's slow approach to Queensland in 2025 created cooler sea temperatures that helped 90 per cent of damaged coral around Lady Elliot Island to recover. Now there's hope of a new spawning event.

items.title: Director Destin Daniel Cretton on making Spider-Man grow up
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has premiered into a very different cinematic landscape than its predecessors, but director Destin Daniel Cretton still sees the light.

items.title: Chinese AI shakes up global markets
items.description: A new wave of cheaper, powerful Chinese AI models are gaining traction and challenging the dominance of US tech giants Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.title: India's 'cockroaches' won. So what happens next?
items.description: The Cockroach Janta Party claims victory following the resignation of India's education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. But is it enough to satisfy India's youth?

items.title: Viral hit The Polygamist raises issues — and eyebrows
items.description: The Netflix show The Polygamist prompts strong reactions online, while opening up some important community discussions around fidelity and addiction.

items.title: 'Somewhat racist': Does the Grammys need an 'Asian' category?
items.description: K-pop powerhouse BTS's decision to boycott the upcoming Grammys after the introduction of an 'Asian' pop prize has prompted questions about the need for a separate category.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Testing your knowledge of Get Smart, Snoopy and liking piña coladas
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right, the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: Infantino's advisor quits as FIFA's World Cup plan triggers backlash
items.description: A senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino resigned in protest at plans to sell a stake in the World Cup.

items.title: In towns where thousands of homes are Airbnbs, renters want a tax
items.description: Homelessness NSW says it is easier to get a holiday rental than a long-term rental — and that needs to change. But the industry says those claims are unfair.

items.title: Gym owner fighting for insurance nearly four years after 2022 floods
items.description: Six businesses in the same regional Victorian street were inundated nearly four years ago, with five having their claims paid and one still fighting its insurer to have the claim covered.

items.title: Gina Rinehart puts ABC on notice over Race Around the World episode
items.description: Hancock Prospecting has formally placed ABC Chair Kim Williams AM, Deputy Chair Lisa Caffery and Managing Director Hugh Marks on notice and foreshadowed possible legal action.

items.title: Sri Lanka sentences officials to death over bombing that killed Australians
items.description: The 2019 Easter Sunday bombings on churches and luxury tourist hotels killed more than 260 people, including two Australians.

items.title: Stowaway school teacher who disguised herself as a boy on a tall ship
items.description: In 1928, Balaklava school teacher Jeanne Day set her eyes on a Finnish tall ship docked at Port Lincoln and decided to disguise herself as a boy for the voyage of a lifetime.

items.title: The people contacting the National Debt Helpline may surprise you
items.description: A record-high number of people are seeking help via the National Debt Helpline, as financial counsellors say anyone can seek support.

items.title: Vertical schools providing a feeling of 'transcendence' for students
items.description: Vertical schools have sprung up in Brisbane over the past six years, occupying a smaller inner-city footprint and providing a unique model for education.
